concepts.partName: Newspapers and the Press in Telangana
concepts.bodyMd:
India's first newspaper was the **Bengal Gazette**, started by **James Augustus Hicky in 1780**. In the Hyderabad State, the Nizam Government's ordinance **Gasti Nishan 53** banned freedom of expression and the press. English, Telugu, and Urdu newspapers were published across the state precisely to create awareness among the people while working around this restriction.

Diverse linguistic communities — Telugu, Marathi, Urdu, and Kannada speakers — lived together in the erstwhile Hyderabad State, though Telugu speakers formed the majority and Urdu held official-language status. In such conditions, learned Telugu individuals took up book publication, library founding, socio-cultural reform movements, and newspaper launches to awaken the public.

### Printing Presses

*   **Brahma Vidya Vilasam Printing Press (1870)** — established by the **Wanaparthy rulers**; the first printing press in the Hyderabad State.
*   In **1875**, a printing press was established at **Gadwal Samsthanam**.

concepts.partName: Early Newspapers of Hyderabad State (Urdu, Persian, English)

|---|---|---|
| Jubdoot-Ul-Akbar | 1833 | One of the earliest newspapers of India; established at Hyderabad. |
| Risala Tabbi | 1859 | A medical journal in Urdu; the first newspaper published in Hyderabad. |
| Octareshfak | 1878 | Published in Parsi language; some scholars consider it the first newspaper in the Nizam State. |
| Deccan Times | 1864 | First English newspaper from Hyderabad; established by Abdul Khader. |
| Hyderabad Recorder | 1885 | English newspaper; the first newspaper banned by the Nizam Government (1892), after it described the British Resident as "Kaizer" and Britain pressured the Nizam to act. |
| Hyderabad Bulletin | 1904 | English-language paper started by Cameroon; despite Nizam-era restrictions, it boldly published news against the government and survived for nearly 50 years. |

**Maulim-e-Niswan (1892)** was started by **Maulvi Mohib Hussain** to propagate reforms for Muslim women; he is known as the father of journalism in Hyderabad and carried the titles "Hyderabad Women's Education Vaithalika" and "Telangana Sir Syed Ahmed Khan."

| Newspaper | Year | Founder/Editor | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shedya Chandrika | 1886 | Munshi Mohammed Musthak Ahmed Malik | Considered by recent researchers, including **Sangishetty Srinivas**, to be the first Telugu newspaper published in Telangana. It was a translation of the Urdu magazine _Punoon_ and provided agricultural information. |
| Deenvarthaman | 1890–91 | Narayana Swamy Mudaliar (Sultan Bazar, Hyderabad) | Per researchers **Rapolu Andhra Bhaskar** and **Veludurthi Manikya Rao**, the first daily Telugu newspaper. Narayana Swamy had earlier run the weekly _Asaf-Ul-Akbar_ from 1878. |
| Hithabodhini | 1913 | Bandaru Srinivasa Sharma | A weekly magazine published from Mahabubnagar; the first Telugu newspaper distributed all over Telangana. Sharma was a Sanskrit scholar and Ayurvedic doctor from Koyala Konda, Mahabub Nagar. The **Atmakuru ruler Sri Rama Bhupala Bahiri Balawant Bahadur** financed the printing machine for this paper. |
| Nilgiri | 1922 | Shabnaveesu Venkatarama Narsimha Rao | The first political weekly magazine in Telangana. The editor also founded a library named "Samskarini" and wrote the poem _Balika Vilapam_. |
| Tenugu Vara Patrika | 27 August 1922 | Oddiraju Sitaramachandra Rao and Oddiraju Raghava Ranga Rao | The Oddiraju brothers printed this paper at their own Inugurthi printing press in Inugurthi village (Mahabubabad district); they had also founded **Vignana Pracharini Sri Grandhamala (1919)** for educational books. |
| Golconda Patrika | 10 May 1926 | Suravaram Pratap Reddy (editor); centred at Nalgonda | Published Political, Economic, Social, and Cultural news of Telangana as a half-weekly (Wednesday and Saturday). Suravaram first wanted to name it _Andhra Patrika_, but the Nizam Government opposed this, so he chose the name "Golconda" instead. In **1947** it became a daily; it was closed in **1966**. |
| Sujatha Patrika | 1927 | Pasumamula Narsimaha Sharma (editor) | Literary monthly magazine from Hyderabad; its name was suggested by **Rayaprolu Subba Rao**. |
| Bhagyanagar Patrika | 1931 | Bhagya Reddy Varma | Founded for the development of Dalits; its front page carried images of Charminar, Mecca Masjid, and Ellora–Ajanta paintings. From 1937 it was renamed **Adi Hindu Newspaper**. |
| Phula Thota Patrika | 1930–35 | Kambampati Appanna Shastri (editor); Hanumakonda | The first children's paper in Telangana. |
| Telugu Talli | 1939 | Rachamalla Satyavati Devi (editor) | A monthly magazine; the first paper published by a woman editor in Telangana. |
| Telangana Patrika | 1942 | Rajgopal Mudaliyar (founder); Bukkapatnam Ramanuja Chary (editor) | The first daily newspaper from Telangana. |
| Kakatiya Vaara Patrika | 1946 | P.V. Narasimha Rao (founder); Pamulaparthi Sadashiva Rao (editor) | — |
| Shoba | 1947 | Devulapalli Ramanuja Rao | A literary monthly magazine. Devulapalli also ran a secret newspaper from Kurnool titled "State Congress Vartha Sanchika" in 1947. |

### Nilgiri–Tenugu Patrika Rivalry

The **Nilgiri Patrika**, founded in **1922** by editor **Shabnaveesu Venkatarama Narasimha Rao**, was published from **Nalgonda** as the first fully-fledged political weekly in Telangana. Just three days after Nilgiri began, on **27 August 1922**, the **Oddiraju brothers** launched **Tenugu Patrika** from **Inugurthi** in the Manukota taluka.

Because Nilgiri was centred in Nalgonda rather than at the district's administrative headquarters, Tenugu Patrika enjoyed some regional advantage, being published from a village that was itself gaining prominence. However, this created printing difficulties for Tenugu Patrika: since the press was village-based, it struggled to find people who could work the printing machinery — local youths had to be trained specifically for the task — and readers had to arrange postage from Mahabubabad to receive their copies.

There being no radio or television at the time, newspapers were the sole channel through which people learned of national events, and news itself did not travel quickly. Because of this, newspapers depended on the nearest railway station to receive dispatches — someone even had to fetch coastal/overseas news via a personal contact.

Since editorial responsibility for Tenugu Patrika rested solely with the Oddiraju brothers, both had to write content themselves regardless of who was available, and with a limited subscriber base, running the paper for **five years** from such a small village was regarded as a remarkably bold achievement. Alongside publishing the paper, the Oddiraju brothers also ran a book series called **Vignana Pracharini Grandhamala**.

**Nilgiri Patrika** was edited with great competence by **Shabnaveesu Ramanarasimha Rao** until **1925**. Prominent contemporary leaders — **Madapati Hanumantha Rao**, **Bandaru Ramakrishna Rao**, and **Pulijala Rangarao**, among others — contributed poems and essays on various subjects to this paper.

Around this time, Nilgiri refused to publish a sensational story written by **Gudipati Venkatachalam**; Shabnaveesu's decision to reject it itself created a stir. The pioneer of the Andhra movement, **Ramanarasimha Rao**, died in **1929**.

### Suravaram Pratap Reddy and Golconda Patrika

**Suravaram Pratap Reddy** awakened the Telangana public continuously through the **Golconda Patrika** from **1926 to 1946**. It was initially a bi-weekly with outstanding editorials that were a thorn in the side of the Nizam government; it became a daily in **1947**, with Prataparao (Pratap Reddy) as editor throughout, an editorship he never relinquished.

Until Golconda Patrika emerged, the library movement, the Andhra movement, and papers such as Nilgiri and Tenugu Patrika had been mutually dependent for survival. In **1923**, **Mudigonda Veerabhadra Sastry** started a monthly magazine titled _Shaiva Pracharini_ from Warangal; in that period, Tenugu Patrika and Shaiva Pracharini were engaged in a spirited (healthy) rivalry.

### Sujatha, Andhrakesari, Deshabandhu and Related Papers

**Sujatha**, edited by **P.N. Sarma**, concluded with its fourth issue's first number in **1927**. In **1924**, **Adusumilli Dattatreya Sarma** started a weekly paper, _Andhrakesari_, in the Andhra-Telugu language from Secunderabad; it ran for **five years**. The monthly _Deshabandhu_, from Vaddepalli village of Atraf-e-Balda district, was run for three years by **Bellamkonda Ramanujacharyulu** and his brother **Narasimhacharyulu** together.

**B.N. Sarma**, a resident of Ramannapet taluka, Nalgonda district, was proficient in Telugu, Sanskrit, and English. He trained in journalism under Nilgiri Patrika editors **Shabnaveesu Venkatarama Narasimha Rao** and **Madapati Hanumantha Rao**.

When the Nizam government harassed him with a battery of legal questions over his paper's printing decisions, he could not bear it, moved to Bezwada, and ran a paper called _Andhravani_ there for five years; it achieved wide circulation, and the street where its office stood is still called "Andhravani Street." Sarma, who worked at many papers, died in **1970**.

### Ramanujacharyulu and the "Telangana" Daily

In **1929**, **Bukkapatnam Ramanujacharyulu** started the **Hyderabad Bulletin** paper in Hyderabad city. He was the pioneer who first introduced English and Telugu newspaper publication in Telangana.

In **1942**, the **Telangana** daily was published under his editorship; it featured a daily "Charminar Gossip" column. It disclosed the secrets of Nawabi-era administrative offices and high officialdom, which readers eagerly consumed the next day. He was skilled in both English and Telugu writing.

He later joined his friend and colleague **Rajagopal** to start the **Deccan Chronicle** weekly in **1937**, of which he was the editor; it became a daily in **1939**. After his ties with Deccan Chronicle ended, he started an evening paper called **Garrison**.

In **1947** he started the English daily **Daily News**, but died within a month of its launch.

### Bhagyanagar Patrika and Adi Hindu Patrika

In **1925**, the prominent social-reform figure **Bhagya Reddy** established the **Bhagyanagar Patrika**. When Bhagya Reddy fell ill and had to leave for Mysore, the paper was discontinued.

After recovering and returning from Mysore, he restarted it, in the cause of Harijan upliftment, as the weekly **Adi Hindu Patrika**. This paper discussed many political issues and championed the political movements of the Nizam-era public.

### Other Papers of the 1920s–1940s

The **Vibhuti** paper was run under the editorship of **Veerabhadra Sharma**. The **Shobha** paper, run from Warangal under the editorship of **Devulapalli Ramanujarao**, was a prominent literary paper but had to close within a single year due to financial constraints.

Between **1938 and 1945**, few new papers emerged, owing to the Nizam government's severe restrictions on freedom of speech. In **1945**, **Challa Subbarao** started a Telugu monthly called **Tarani**. The prominent Urdu paper _Payam_'s editor **Khwaja Abdul Gaffar** started a Telugu paper, **Sandesham**; it ran for only six months.

| Newspaper | Year | Founder/Editor | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Payam | 1935 | Khaji Abdul Gaffar | An Urdu daily that supported the independence struggle of the Nizam's subjects. |
| Rayyat | 1927 | Mandamula Narsingh Rao | An Urdu weekly ("Rayyat" means a farmer); it informed national leaders of the anti-Nizam movement in Hyderabad, demanded a responsible government in the Nizam State, and fought for people's rights. **Shoebullah Khan**, later editor of _Imroze_, initially worked here. |
| Imroze | 1947 | Shoebullah Khan | An Urdu weekly ("Imroze" means fire). Shoebullah began his career at the Urdu weekly _Tej_, then worked at _Rayyat_ before starting Imroze, through which he criticised the Razakars and wrote editorials advocating Hyderabad's merger into the Indian Union. As a result, he was murdered by the Razakars on **20 August 1948**. |
| Rahbar-e-Deccan | — | Ahmed Mohinuddin and Abdullahkhan (editors) | Supported by the MIM party. |
| Meezan | 1944 | Gulam Mohammed (Gulam Alauddin) of Calcutta | The word "Meezan" is Arabic for "the balance." It was the first paper in Telangana published in three languages — Telugu, English, and Urdu — and the first daily newspaper to run serialised novels. |

### Meezan's Structure

Meezan's Urdu edition supported the Razakars, its English edition supported the Nizam, and its Telugu edition supported communists and other radicals. The Telugu edition's editor was **Adavi Bapiraju**, with **Vidwan Viswam** as sub-editor.

Adavi Bapiraju published stories and songs by **Avula Pichaiah** of Suryapet, and his own serialised novels — _Himabindu_, _Gona Gannareddy_, and _Toofan_ — appeared in Meezan. Contributors to the paper included **Tirumala Ramachandra**, **Rachakonda Krishnamurthy**, **Srinivasa Chakravarti**, and **Bommakanti Subbarao**. Bapiraju's own columns "Dhoopadeepalu" and "Mirchi Masala" entertained and informed readers.

Meezan ran for three years; as Razakar atrocities intensified across the state, Bapiraju resigned his editorial duties on **7 August 1947**.

**Vatan News (Momibbe Vatan)** was founded by **Mustafa Qadri**: at a time when the pro-Nizam news agency **Deccan News** was disseminating pro-government propaganda, Qadri — a critic of Muslim fundamentalism — started the news agency **Vatan News** and its paper _Momibbe Vatan_ ("patriot") to publish unbiased news. **Ganapati Rao Akhilekar**, through his agency **Modern News**, similarly circulated the pro-government news supplied by Deccan News agency's _Deccan News_.

**Masawat** (meaning "Equality") was an Urdu weekly started by **Prem Kumar**, Vice-President of the Hyderabad Depressed Classes Federation.

### Telugu Book Distribution under the Nizam

During the Nizam period, besides the **Srikrishna Devaraya Andhra Basha Nilayam** in Hyderabad, there was only one Telugu book stall in the entire Nizam State, run by **Nampalli Gouri Shankar Sharma**. He distributed Telugu books across the state and, for this service, was regarded as a "language servant."

concepts.partName: Pioneers of Research and Literature in Telangana
concepts.bodyMd:
### Komarraju Venkat Laxman Rao (1876–1923)

*   The first person to conduct research into Telangana's literature.
*   Born in **Penuganchiprolu** (Krishna district); later settled in **Bhuvanagiri**, Telangana.
*   Worked as Diwan to the Munagala Zamindar, **Raja Nayani Venkat Ranga Rao**.
*   Established several libraries and authored many books; proved that the ancient city of **Ekasila** was not Ontimetta in Kadapa district but was, in fact, **Orugallu** (Warangal).
*   **Books:** Shivaji Chritra, Haindava Chakravarthulu, Hindu Mahayugam, Mohammadain Mahayugam, and Andhra Vignana Sarvasvam (the first Vignana Sarvasvam/encyclopaedia in Telugu).
*   In **1910**, he wrote Telangana's first short story, _Ebadivella Bheramu_, though some scholars instead credit **Madapati Hanumanthrao's** 1912 story _Hrudaya Shalyamu_ as the first.

### Manavalli Ramakrishna Kavi (1866–1957)

*   Served as personal secretary to the Wanaparthy ruler **Sawai Rameshwar Rao Bahadur**.
*   Collected inscriptions and published them as _Lithic Records of Hyderabad State_.
*   Published ancient texts in a series titled _Visrutha Kavulu_.

### Seshadri Ramana Kavulu

*   Established the **Historical Research Council** (Charitraka Parishodaka Mandali) at Hanumakonda.
*   In **1931**, organized the **Akhilandhra Historical Conference**.
*   Key literary work: _Andhra Veerulu_.

### Adiraju Veerabhadra Rao

*   Born in **Dendukur** (Madhira Taluka, Khammam district); given shelter in Hyderabad by **Ravi Chettu Ranga Rao**.
*   Established the **Andhra Research Council** (Andhra Parishodaka Mandali) under the Andhra Jana Kendra Sangam.
*   The first person to give a speech on Hyderabad Radio.
*   Collected Telangana's inscriptions and published two volumes as _Telangana Inscriptions_.
*   **Other writings:** Mana Telanganamu, Ratnaprabha, Chaitanyamu, Jeevita Charitavali, Lalitha Kalavali, Navvula Puvvulu, and _Ancient Cities of Andhra_ — covering the history of twelve ancient cities including Kondapur, Kolanupaka, Anegondi, Alampur, Bhuvangiri, Rachakonda, Warangal, and Pangal.

### Suravaram Pratap Reddy (1896–1953)

*   Born in **Itikyalapadu** village, Jogulamba Gadwal district.
*   Because contemporary Andhra poets claimed Telangana had no poets, he was moved to research Telangana's literature.
*   In **1934**, compiled **Golconda Kavulu**, a list of the works of **354 Telangana poets**, to prove that Telangana possessed a rich literary and poetic tradition.
*   Wrote _Andhrulu Saanghika Charitra_, a social history of the Telugu people, which won the **Kendra Sahitya Academy Puraskaram in 1955** — making him the **first Telugu poet** to receive the award.
*   Autobiography: _Svavishaya Sangraham_.
*   Started and edited the **Golconda Patrika** in 1926; founded the **Vigyana Vardhini Parishad** in 1941; ran **Prajavani Patrika** in 1951–52.
*   Wrote under several pen names, including Chitra Gupta, Jagam Basavaiah, Vishwamitra, Yugapati, Amrutha Kalasi, Sangrama Simha, Bhava Kabi Ram Murthy, and Bahadur.
*   **Stories:** Mogalayi Kathalu; **comic/satirical writings:** Verrivengalappa, Kavilekattalu.
*   **Research works:** Golconda Kavula Sanchika (1934), Hinduvula Pandugalu (1931), Ramayana Visheshalu (1943), Prapancha Grandalaya Charitra, Lipi Samskaranalu.
*   **Dramas:** Uchchala Vishadamu (based on Kalhana's Rajatarangini), Baktha Tukaram.
*   **Novels:** Arevirulu, Suddantha Katha.
*   **Poetry & Prose:** Sangala Panthulu, Hamsaveera Sambhavam, Padmini, Mohammed Ghazni, Deshanata.
*   In the **first general elections of Hyderabad State (1952)**, he was elected to the legislative assembly (Congress Party) from the Wanaparthy constituency.

### Biruduraju Ramaraju

*   Native of **Devanuru** village, Warangal district.
*   Researched folklore literature; awarded a Ph.D. in Telugu literature by **Osmania University in 1956**.
*   **Literary works:** Maruguna Padina Manikyalu, Charitra Kekkina Charitardulu, Andhra Yogulu.
*   Discovered and researched: Kakatiya Prataparudra's _Usha Ragodhayam_, Sri Krishna Devaraya's _Jambavati Parinayam_, Palkuriki Somanatha's _Panditharadhya Charitra_ and _Basavodaharanam_, Srinatha's _Shiva Ratri Mahatyam_, and Madiki Singanna's _Padma Puranam_.

### Daasarathi Krishnamacharyulu (1925–1987)

*   Born in **Chinnaguduru** village, Warangal district (now in Mahabubabad district).
*   Held a B.A. in English literature from Osmania University; worked as a teacher and Akashavani speaker.
*   Served as **Court Poet of Andhra Pradesh, 1977–83**; titles: Kalaprapurna and Abhyudhaya Bhaavi.
*   Won the **Kendra Sahitya Academy Award in 1974** for _Timiramto Samaram_ ("Fight against Darkness").
*   As part of the **Andhra Mahasabha**, travelled village to village to raise public awareness; arrested by the Nizam government in **1947** and imprisoned at **Induru Fort Jail, Nizamabad** for his role in the public agitation — along with poet **Vattikota Alwar Swamy**. He used to write poems on the jail walls with charcoal (meant for brushing teeth); police mistakenly attributed and punished Vattikota for these.
*   Founded **Telangana Rachayithala Sangam** (Telangana Writers' Association) in **1953** and served as its president.
*   Entered cinema in **1961**, writing lyrics for _Iddaru Mitrulu_.
*   **Literary works:** Agnidhara (on the Telangana Armed Struggle), Rudraveena, Navami, Punarnavam, Mahashilpi Jakkanna, Mahandrodyamam, Kavitha Pushpakam, Timiramto Samaram, Amruthabishekam, Mahaboddhi, Ghalib Geethalu, Alochanalochanalu. He received the **Andhra Pradesh Sahitya Academy Award** for _Kavitha Pushpakam_.
*   The **1st Daasarathi Krishnamacharya Award** was given by the Telangana Government to **Tirumala Srinivasa Charyulu** (Karimnagar).

### Daasarathi Rangacharya (1928–2015)

*   Born in **Chinnaguduru** village, Warangal district; brother of Daasarathi Krishnamacharya.
*   Expelled from school in the 6th standard for organising a strike (wearing Gandhiji's cap instead of the Nizam-prescribed uniform); worked as a teacher from **1951–57**.
*   Known as **Akshara Vachaspathi** and **Telangana Karadeepika**; participated in the Telangana Armed Struggle.
*   Autobiography: _Jeevanayanam_.
*   **Literary works:** Chillara Devullu, Modugupulu, Janapadam, Maya Jalataru, Saratalpam, Ranunnadi Edi Nizam, Sri Madramayanam, Sri Mahabharatam — with **Chillara Devullu** and **Modugupulu** the most prominent, describing the Telangana Struggles and the conditions before Telangana's liberation.
*   **Modugu Pulu** won the Kendra Sahitya Academy Award; **Chillera Devullu** won a National Literature Award and was adapted into a successful film directed by **T. Madhava Rao**.
*   Translated all four Vedas into Telugu, and translated the Urdu classic _Umrao Jaan_ into Telugu.

### Vattikota Alwar Swamy (1915–1961)

*   Born in **Cheruvu Madaram** village, Nalgonda district; called **Telangana Vaithalika** (Pioneer) and **Telangana Gorki**.
*   Raised by his teacher **Seetharama Rao** after his father's early death.
*   Jailed for participation in the **Quit India Movement (1942–43)**; came under communist influence and turned communist thereafter.
*   Active in the library movement; fought against the Nizam and, for this, was imprisoned at **Induru Jail, Nizamabad, 1946–1951**, under rigorous punishment.
*   **Literary works:** Jailu Lopala (life inside jail), Prajala Manishi (conditions of Telangana people, 1934–38), Gangu (Telangana people's history, 1940–45), Telangana, Chinnappude, Ramappa Rabhasa (against social evils; published in _Telugu Vidyarthi_ patrika from Machilipatnam).
*   Established **Deshoddaraka Grandhamala**, whose first published book was Suravaram Pratap Reddy's _Prajadhikaramulu_.

### Devulapalli Ramanuja Rao (1917–1993)

*   Born in **Desai peta** village, Warangal district.
*   Ran the newspaper _Shobha_ (literary monthly); served as President of the **Andhra Saraswatha Parishad** in 1953 (held at Alampur).
*   **Literary works:** History of Telangana Armed Struggle, Telanganalo Jathiyodhyamalu, Saraswatha Navaneetham, Telugu Seemalo Samskrutika Punarjeevam, Hyderabad Swatantryodhyamam, Fifty Years of Remembrance (1929–79), Tenugu Literature, Veguchukkalu, Upanyasa Toranam, Kavya Mala, Talupula Dumaramu, Five Year Plans, My Radio Speeches, Our Village – Orugallu, Mana Desham – Telugu Seema.

### Gadiyaram Ramakrishna Sharma

*   Autobiography **Satapatram** ("Hundred Petals") won the **Kendra Sahitya Academy Award in 2007**, posthumously.
*   **Literary works:** Madhava Vidyaranya Charitra, Alampura Kshethra Charitra, Veera Gadalu, Vignana Vallari, Dasharupaka Saram, Panchajanyam, Mana Vastu Sampada, Umamaheshwara Charitra.

### Dr. C. Narayana Reddy (1931–2017)

*   Born in **1931** at **Hanumajipet**, Karimnagar district.
*   Won the prestigious **Jnanpith Award in 1988** for _Viswambhara_, becoming the **first person from Telangana** to receive it.
*   Held a post-graduate degree and doctorate in Telugu literature from **Osmania University**, later becoming a professor there.
*   **Awards:** 1973 – Kendra Sahitya Academy Award (for _Mantalu-Manavudu_); 1977 – Padma Shri; 1978 – Kala Prapoorna; 1988 – Jnanpith Award; 1992 – Padma Bhushan; 2014 – Kendra Sahitya Academy Fellowship.
*   **Literary works:** Navvani Puvvu (1953, his first work), Ruthu Chakram, Vyakthithvam, Karpura Vasantha Rayalu, Bhugolamantha Manishi, Mattimanishi Aakasham, Mukhamukhi, Manishi–Chiluka, Ajanta Sundari, Vishwambhara, Kalam Sakshiga, Mantalu Manavudu, Nagarjuna Sagar, Bhoomika, Marpu Na Teerpu, Ramappa, Divvela Muvvalu.
*   Entered the film industry as a lyricist with _Gulebhakavali Katha_ (1962), going on to write more than **3,000 songs**; became widely popular with the song "Nannu Dochukunduvate Vannela Dorasani."

### Other Literary Figures

*   **Tadakamalla Krishna Rao (1830–1890)** wrote Telangana's first novel, _Kambukandhara Charitra_.
*   **Palla Durgaiah (1916–1983)** wrote Gangiredhu (Abull), Prabhanda Vajmaya Vikasam, and Palavelli. Together with Gangula Sai Reddy's _Kapu Bidda_ and C. Narayana Reddy's _Ruthu Chakram_, Palla Durgaiah's _Gangireddu_ is treated as part of the modern-dialect **Kavyatrayam** (trio of poetic works).
*   **Bunna Ilaiah** wrote the research work _Telangana Sahitya Samasthalu_, documenting the founding history of literary centres from Adilabad to Hyderabad, and depicted the lives of Telangana's people in the story _Kaluva Mallaiah_. His other works include _Nippu Kanika_ and _Rahasya Chitram_.

faqs.e: Established in 1870 by the Wanaparthy rulers.

faqs.q: In which year was a printing press established at Gadwal Samsthanam?
Which of the following was the first English newspaper published from Hyderabad?
faqs.e: Established in 1864 by Abdul Khader.

faqs.q: Which newspaper is regarded as the first newspaper published in Hyderabad?
faqs.e: A medical journal published in Urdu, established in 1859.

faqs.q:
Consider the following pairs:
(I) Jubdoot-Ul-Akbar – 1833
(II) Deccan Times – 1878
(III) Octareshfak – 1864
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
faqs.e: Deccan Times was established in 1864 and Octareshfak in 1878 — the years in pairs (II) and (III) are interchanged.

faqs.q: Who established the Deccan Times, the first English newspaper from Hyderabad?

Consider the following statements regarding the Hyderabad Recorder:
(I) It was the first newspaper banned by the Nizam Government.
(II) It described the British Resident as "Kaizer."
(III) It was an Urdu newspaper.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
faqs.e: Hyderabad Recorder was an English newspaper, not Urdu; it was banned in 1892 after describing the British Resident as "Kaizer," which drew British pressure on the Nizam.

faqs.q: In which language was the newspaper Octareshfak published?
faqs.e: Some consider it the first newspaper in the Nizam State.

faqs.q: Who started the Hyderabad Bulletin in 1904, which rendered service for nearly 50 years despite Nizam-era restrictions?
Who is known as the "father of journalism in Hyderabad"?
faqs.e: He started Maulim-e-Niswan (1892) to propagate reforms for Muslim women, and carried the titles "Hyderabad Women's Education Vaithalika" and "Telangana Sir Syed Ahmed Khan."

faqs.q: Which is considered, according to researcher Sangishetty Srinivas, the first Telugu newspaper published in Telangana?
faqs.e: Founded in 1886 by Munshi Mohammed Musthak Ahmed Malik as a translation of the Urdu magazine Punoon; it provided agricultural information.

faqs.q: Which is regarded, per researchers Rapolu Andhra Bhaskar and Veludurthi Manikya Rao, as the first daily Telugu newspaper?
faqs.e: Started in 1890–91 by Narayana Swamy Mudaliar in Sultan Bazar, Hyderabad.

faqs.q: Who founded Hithabodhini, the first Telugu newspaper distributed all over Telangana?
faqs.e: Established in 1913 as a weekly magazine from Mahabubnagar; the Atmakuru ruler Sri Rama Bhupala Bahiri Balawant Bahadur financed the printing machine for it.

faqs.q: Which was the first political weekly magazine in Telangana?
faqs.e: Founded in 1922, with Shabnaveesu Venkatarama Narsimha Rao as editor.

faqs.q: Which library did Shabnaveesu Venkatarama Narasimha Rao, editor of Nilgiri Patrika, establish?
Who were the founders of Tenugu Vara Patrika?

options.a: Bandaru Srinivasa Sharma and Narayana Swamy Mudaliar
options.b: Oddiraju Sitaramachandra Rao and Oddiraju Raghava Ranga Rao
options.c: Devulapalli Ramanuja Rao and P.V. Narasimha Rao
options.d: Suravaram Pratap Reddy and Rajgopal Mudaliyar

faqs.a: Oddiraju Sitaramachandra Rao and Oddiraju Raghava Ranga Rao
faqs.e: They printed the paper at their own Inugurthi printing press in Inugurthi village, Mahabubabad district.

faqs.q: On which date was Tenugu Vara Patrika started?
Which book series did the Oddiraju brothers establish in 1919 for publishing educational books?
Who served as the editor of Golconda Patrika from its establishment?
faqs.e: The paper became a daily in 1947 and was closed in 1966.

faqs.q: What name did Suravaram Pratap Reddy originally intend to give the paper that eventually became Golconda Patrika?
faqs.e: The Nizam Government opposed this name, so he chose "Golconda" instead.

faqs.q: Who was the editor of Sujatha Patrika, a literary monthly magazine started in 1927?
faqs.e: The name "Sujatha" was suggested by Rayaprolu Subba Rao.

faqs.q: Who founded the Bhagyanagar Patrika in 1931 for the development of Dalits?
faqs.e: From 1937 the paper was renamed the Adi Hindu Newspaper.

faqs.q: Which was the first children's paper in Telangana?
faqs.e: Edited by Kambampati Appanna Shastri and published from Hanumakonda between 1930–35.

faqs.q: Which was the first paper published by a woman editor in Telangana?
faqs.e: Edited by Rachamalla Satyavati Devi; a monthly magazine started in 1939.

faqs.q: Which was the first daily newspaper from Telangana?
faqs.e: Founded by Rajgopal Mudaliyar in 1942, with Bukkapatnam Ramanuja Chary as editor.

faqs.q: Who founded the Kakatiya Vaara Patrika in 1946?
faqs.e: Pamulaparthi Sadashiva Rao served as its editor.

faqs.q: Who founded Shoba, a literary monthly magazine started in 1947?
faqs.e: He also ran a secret newspaper called "State Congress Vartha Sanchika" from Kurnool in 1947.

faqs.q: Which taluka's village, Inugurthi, served as the base of the Oddiraju brothers' printing press for Tenugu Vara Patrika?
Who among the following contributed poems and essays to Nilgiri Patrika?
faqs.e: Bandaru Ramakrishna Rao and Pulijala Rangarao also contributed to the paper.

faqs.q: Whose sensational story did Nilgiri Patrika refuse to publish, creating a stir?
Who started the monthly magazine Shaiva Pracharini from Warangal in 1923?
faqs.e: This paper engaged in a spirited rivalry with Tenugu Patrika during that period.

faqs.q: Which two papers were engaged in a spirited rivalry after 1923?
Who started the weekly paper Andhrakesari from Secunderabad in 1924?
faqs.e: The paper ran for five years.

faqs.q: Deshabandhu, a monthly magazine tagged "Andhra Vignana Prabodha," was run by Bellamkonda Narasimha Charyulu and which brother?
faqs.e: The paper ran for three years from Vaddepalli village, Atraf-e-Balda district.

faqs.q: B.N. Sarma trained in journalism under which two editors of Nilgiri Patrika?

options.a: Suravaram Pratap Reddy and Bukkapatnam Ramanujacharyulu
options.b: Shabnaveesu Venkatarama Narasimha Rao and Madapati Hanumantha Rao
options.d: Pasumamula Narsimaha Sharma and Rayaprolu Subba Rao

faqs.a: Shabnaveesu Venkatarama Narasimha Rao and Madapati Hanumantha Rao

faqs.q: Which paper did B.N. Sarma run from Bezwada for five years after moving there due to Nizam government harassment?
faqs.e: The street where its office stood is still called "Andhravani Street"; Sarma died in 1970.

faqs.q: Who started the Hyderabad Bulletin paper in Hyderabad city in 1929?
faqs.e: He is credited as the pioneer who first introduced English and Telugu newspaper publication in Telangana.

faqs.q: Which daily column featured in the Telangana daily, published in 1942 under Bukkapatnam Ramanujacharyulu's editorship?
Ramanujacharyulu joined his friend Rajagopal to start which weekly in 1937, which became a daily in 1939?
What was the name of the evening paper started by Ramanujacharyulu after his ties with Deccan Chronicle ended?
Which English daily, started by Ramanujacharyulu in 1947, saw him die within a month of its launch?
Who founded the Bhagyanagar Patrika, which was discontinued when he fell ill and left for Mysore, then restarted as Adi Hindu Patrika upon his return?
Under whose editorship was the Vibhuti paper run?
Who started the Telugu monthly Tarani in 1945?
Khwaja Abdul Gaffar, editor of the Urdu paper Payam, also started which Telugu paper that ran for only six months?
Which Urdu daily, started by Khaji Abdul Gaffar in 1935, supported the independence struggle of the Nizam's subjects?
Who started and edited the Urdu weekly Rayyat in 1927, which fought for people's rights against the Nizam?
faqs.e: "Rayyat" means a farmer; Shoebullah Khan, later editor of Imroze, initially worked here.

faqs.q: Who started the Urdu weekly Imroze in 1947, meaning "fire"?

Consider the following statements about Shoebullah Khan:
(I) He began his journalism career at the Urdu weekly Tej.
(II) He worked at Rayyat before starting Imroze.
(III) He advocated Hyderabad's merger into the Indian Union through his editorials.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
Who were the editors of Rahbar-e-Deccan, a paper supported by the MIM party?

options.b: Mustafa Qadri and Ganapati Rao Akhilekar
options.d: Shoebullah Khan and Mandamula Narsingh Rao

faqs.q: Who founded the paper Meezan in 1944, the first paper in Telangana published in three languages?
faqs.e: He belonged to Calcutta; "Meezan" is an Arabic word meaning "the balance." It was published in Telugu, English, and Urdu, and was the first daily newspaper to run serialised novels.

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements about the political alignment of Meezan's editions:
(I) The Urdu edition supported the Razakars.
(II) The English edition supported the Nizam.
(III) The Telugu edition supported communists and other radicals.
Which of the above is/are correct?
Who was the editor of Meezan's Telugu edition?
faqs.e: Vidwan Viswam served as sub-editor; Bapiraju's own serialised novels Himabindu, Gona Gannareddy, and Toofan appeared in the paper.

faqs.q: Who founded the news agency Vatan News and its paper Momibbe Vatan to counter the pro-Nizam Deccan News agency?
faqs.e: Mustafa Qadri was a critic of Muslim fundamentalism; "Momibbe Vatan" means "patriot."

faqs.q: Through which agency did Ganapati Rao Akhilekar circulate the pro-government news supplied by Deccan News agency?
Who started the Urdu weekly Masawat, meaning "Equality"?
faqs.e: He was the Vice-President of the Hyderabad Depressed Classes Federation.

faqs.q: Besides the Srikrishna Devaraya Andhra Basha Nilayam, who ran the only Telugu book stall in the entire Nizam State?
faqs.e: He distributed Telugu books across the state and was regarded as a "language servant" for this service.

faqs.q: Which paper, started in 1917, was published on behalf of the Divine Life Society from Secunderabad?
faqs.e: Its editor was Swamy Venkat Rao.

faqs.q: Which paper is considered the first fortnightly paper in Telangana, run by Revenue officers from Warangal?
faqs.e: Started in 1925.

faqs.q: Kashtukar (1931), a peasant journal published from Dablipura of Hyderabad, was notable for being published in which two languages?
faqs.e: It was founded by Mohammad Abdul Razaq Bismil.

faqs.q: Who founded the medical/health-related paper Vaidyakala in 1931?
Who started the paper Deccan Kesari in 1934?
Who started the paper Andhra Kesari in 1941?
Who ran the paper Prajavani in 1951?
The paper Navayuga (1954) was run by which organization?
Who ran the Hyderabad Weekly paper?
Who was the first person to conduct research into Telangana's literature?
faqs.e: Born 1876, died 1923; born in Penuganchiprolu, Krishna district, and later settled in Bhuvanagiri, Telangana.

faqs.q: Komarraju Venkat Laxman Rao worked as Diwan to which Zamindar?

options.a: Wanaparthy ruler Sawai Rameshwar Rao Bahadur
options.b: Munagala Zamindar Raja Nayani Venkat Ranga Rao
options.c: Atmakuru ruler Sri Rama Bhupala Bahiri Balawant Bahadur

faqs.a: Munagala Zamindar Raja Nayani Venkat Ranga Rao

faqs.q: Komarraju Venkat Laxman Rao proved that the ancient city of Ekasila was actually which city?
faqs.e: Some had wrongly identified Ekasila as Ontimetta in Kadapa district.

faqs.q: Which book by Komarraju Venkat Laxman Rao is described as the first Vignana Sarvasvam (encyclopaedia) in Telugu?

Consider the following statements regarding Telangana's first short story:
(I) Komarraju Laxman Rao wrote "Ebadivella Bheramu" in 1910.
(II) Some scholars instead credit Madapati Hanumanthrao's 1912 story "Hrudaya Shalyamu" as the first.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
faqs.e: This is a genuine scholarly disagreement over which story holds the distinction of being first.

faqs.q: Seshadri Ramana Kavulu established the Historical Research Council (Charitraka Parishodaka Mandali) at which place?
Adiraju Veerabhadra Rao established the Andhra Research Council (Andhra Parishodaka Mandali) under which organization?
Which book by Suravaram Pratap Reddy, a social history of the Telugu people, won the Kendra Sahitya Academy Puraskaram in 1955?
faqs.e: This made Suravaram Pratap Reddy the first Telugu poet to receive the Kendra Sahitya Academy award.

faqs.q: What is the title of Suravaram Pratap Reddy's autobiography?
In which village was Suravaram Pratap Reddy born?
faqs.e: In Jogulamba Gadwal district; he lived from 1896 to 1953.

faqs.q: Which organization did Suravaram Pratap Reddy found in 1941?
Which of the following is a pen name used by Suravaram Pratap Reddy?
faqs.e: His other pen names included Jagam Basavaiah, Vishwamitra, Yugapati, Amrutha Kalasi, Sangrama Simha, Bhava Kabi Ram Murthy, and Bahadur.

faqs.q: Which drama by Suravaram Pratap Reddy is based on the story of Kalhana in Rajatarangini?
In the first general elections of Hyderabad State in 1952, Suravaram Pratap Reddy was elected to the legislative assembly from which constituency?
faqs.e: He contested and won as a Congress Party candidate.

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements about Suravaram Pratap Reddy's writings:
(I) Mogalayi Kathalu is a collection of his stories.
(II) Verrivengalappa and Kavilekattalu are his comic/satirical writings.
(III) He wrote the novels Arevirulu and Suddantha Katha.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
In which district was Biruduraju Ramaraju, a researcher in folklore literature, a native?
faqs.e: He was native to Devanuru village.

faqs.q: Which university conferred a Ph.D. in Telugu literature on Biruduraju Ramaraju in 1956?
Biruduraju Ramaraju discovered and researched Kakatiya Prataparudra's work titled:

Consider the following pairs of works discovered/researched by Biruduraju Ramaraju and their authors:
(I) Jambavati Parinayam – Sri Krishna Devaraya
(II) Panditharadhya Charitra – Palkuriki Somanatha
(III) Shiva Ratri Mahatyam – Madiki Singanna
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
faqs.e: Shiva Ratri Mahatyam was authored by Srinatha, not Madiki Singanna; Madiki Singanna authored Padma Puranam.

faqs.q: In which village was Daasarathi Krishnamacharyulu born?
faqs.e: In Warangal district (now in Mahabubabad district); he lived from 1925 to 1987.

faqs.q: For which work did Daasarathi Krishnamacharyulu win the Kendra Sahitya Academy Award in 1974?
faqs.e: The title means "Fight against Darkness."

faqs.q: Along with which poet was Daasarathi Krishnamacharyulu arrested in 1947 and imprisoned at Induru Fort Jail, Nizamabad?
faqs.e: While in jail, Daasarathi wrote poems on the walls using charcoal, and police mistakenly punished Vattikota for these.

faqs.q: In which year did Daasarathi Krishnamacharyulu found the Telangana Rachayithala Sangam (Telangana Writers' Association)?
Daasarathi Krishnamacharyulu entered the cinema field in 1961 by writing lyrics for which film?
Which award did Daasarathi Krishnamacharyulu receive for his work Kavitha Pushpakam?
The 1st Daasarathi Krishnamacharya Award, given by the Telangana Government, was awarded to whom?
faqs.e: He was from Karimnagar.

faqs.q: Daasarathi Rangacharya, brother of Daasarathi Krishnamacharyulu, was expelled from school in which standard for organizing a strike?
faqs.e: He wore Gandhiji's cap instead of the Nizam-prescribed school uniform.

faqs.q: What is Daasarathi Rangacharya known as, alongside "Telangana Karadeepika"?
What is the title of Daasarathi Rangacharya's autobiography?
Which award did Daasarathi Rangacharya's work "Modugu Pulu" win?
Which award did Daasarathi Rangacharya's work "Chillera Devullu" win, and it was also adapted into a successful film?
faqs.e: The film adaptation was directed by T. Madhava Rao.

faqs.q: Which two Telugu epics did Daasarathi Rangacharya translate, along with all four Vedas?
faqs.e: He also translated the Urdu classic Umrao Jaan into Telugu.

faqs.q: In which district was Daasarathi Rangacharya, like his brother Krishnamacharyulu, born?
faqs.e: Both brothers were born in Chinnaguduru village.

faqs.q: Which of the following is NOT among Daasarathi Rangacharya's literary works?
faqs.e: Agnidhara, on the Telangana Armed Struggle, is a work by Daasarathi Krishnamacharyulu, not Daasarathi Rangacharya.

faqs.q: Which award, given in 1974 for Timiramto Samaram, was won by Daasarathi Krishnamacharyulu?
Which title did Daasarathi Krishnamacharyulu hold, along with "Abhyudhaya Bhaavi"?
What are the two titles by which Vattikota Alwar Swamy is known?

options.d: Telangana Sir Syed Ahmed Khan and Language Servant

faqs.q: Vattikota Alwar Swamy was jailed for his participation in which movement (1942–43)?
faqs.e: He came under communist influence and turned communist thereafter.

faqs.q: Which work by Vattikota Alwar Swamy describes the conditions of Telangana people between 1934 and 1938?
faqs.e: Prajala Manishi means "People's man."

faqs.q: In which publication was Vattikota Alwar Swamy's work "Ramappa Rabhasa," written against social evils, published?
faqs.e: It was distributed from Machilipatnam.

faqs.q: Vattikota Alwar Swamy established which organization, whose first published book was Suravaram Pratap Reddy's "Prajadhikaramulu"?
In which village was Devulapalli Ramanuja Rao born?
faqs.e: In Warangal district; he lived from 1917 to 1993.

faqs.q: Devulapalli Ramanuja Rao served as President of the Andhra Saraswatha Parishad in 1953, held at which place?
Which of the following is a literary work by Devulapalli Ramanuja Rao on the Telangana freedom struggle?

Consider the following statements about Devulapalli Ramanuja Rao's literary works:
(I) Telanganalo Jathiyodhyamalu concerns the Telangana Nationalist Movement.
(II) Telugu Seemalo Samskrutika Punarjeevam concerns cultural revival in Telugu Seema.
(III) Fifty Years of Remembrance covers the period 1929–79.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
What is the title of Gadiyaram Ramakrishna Sharma's autobiography, which won the Kendra Sahitya Academy Award in 2007?
faqs.e: The title means "Hundred Petals"; the award was given posthumously.

faqs.q: Which of the following is a literary work by Gadiyaram Ramakrishna Sharma?
In which village was Dr. Cingi Reddy Narayana Reddy (C. Narayana Reddy) born in 1931?
faqs.e: In Karimnagar district.

faqs.q: For which work did C. Narayana Reddy win the prestigious Jnanpith Award in 1988?
faqs.e: This made him the first person from Telangana to receive the Jnanpith Award.

faqs.q: Which university awarded C. Narayana Reddy his post-graduate degree and doctorate in Telugu literature, where he later became a professor?

Consider the following pairs of C. Narayana Reddy's awards and years:
(I) Kendra Sahitya Academy Award – 1973
(II) Padma Shri – 1977
(III) Padma Bhushan – 1988
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
faqs.e: C. Narayana Reddy received the Jnanpith Award in 1988 and Padma Bhushan in 1992 — the pairing of Padma Bhushan with 1988 is incorrect.

faqs.q: Which was C. Narayana Reddy's first literary work, published in 1953?
C. Narayana Reddy entered the film industry as a lyricist in 1962 with which film?
faqs.e: He went on to write more than 3,000 songs and became widely popular with "Nannu Dochukunduvate Vannela Dorasani."

faqs.q: In which year did C. Narayana Reddy receive the Kendra Sahitya Academy Fellowship?
Who wrote Telangana's first novel, "Kambukandhara Charitra"?
faqs.e: He lived from 1830 to 1890.

faqs.q: Which of the following is a literary work by Palla Durgaiah (1916–1983)?
faqs.e: Also known as "Gangiredhu" (Abull); his other works are Prabhanda Vajmaya Vikasam and Palavelli.

faqs.q:
Consider the following pairs of works belonging to the modern-dialect "Kavyatrayam" (trio of poetic works):
(I) Gangula Sai Reddy – Kapu Bidda
(II) Palla Durgaiah – Gangireddu
(III) C. Narayana Reddy – Ruthu Chakram
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
Bunna Ilaiah's research book "Telangana Sahitya Samasthalu" documents the founding history of literary centres spanning which region?
In which story did Bunna Ilaiah depict the lives of Telangana's people?
faqs.e: His other works include Nippu Kanika and Rahasya Chitram.

faqs.q: Who is credited with writing all four Vedas' translation into Telugu?
Which raised Vattikota Alwar Swamy after his father's early death?
Which work by Vattikota Alwar Swamy covers Telangana people's history from 1940–45?
Devulapalli Ramanuja Rao's work "Mana Desham" is subtitled with which region's name?
faqs.e: The full title is "Mana desham – Telugu Seema"; he also wrote "Our Village – Orugallu."

faqs.q: Which award, given in 1977, did C. Narayana Reddy receive before the Jnanpith Award in 1988?
faqs.e: He received Padma Shri in 1977 and Kala Prapoorna in 1978, prior to the Jnanpith Award in 1988.
